core_obligations: Set up the property P (proof lines 17096-17117): starting from a commutative diagram exhibiting the failure of BC(f, n, q), define P(T') for quasi-compact and quasi-separated T' over T to mean that the base change map fails to be an isomorphism for the pullback of the given sheaf F, so that P(T) holds.

Check the thickening-invariance (proof lines 17161-17164): condition (1) of the formal argument lemma holds for P because the etale topology of a scheme and of a thickening of that scheme coincide, which is the topological invariance result of the same chapter.

Check the limit-stability (proof lines 17167-17201): for an inverse system T_i with affine transition morphisms and limit T', the identification of the pullbacks of F along the transition maps shows that P(T') holds whenever P(T_i) holds for all i.

Check the decomposition step (proof lines 17204-17293): for T' with P(T') and a closed subscheme Z with quasi-compact complement V, the author shows that the failure persists either on V or on Z, which is condition (3).

Conclude (by the formal argument lemma out of the counted spans, as the author does): the three conditions put the existence of a field-valued point Spec(K) -> T with P(Spec(K)) within the scope of the formal argument, which yields the commutative diagram of the statement together with the sheaf on Spec(K) annihilated by n witnessing the failure of base change in degree q.
The counted statement carries a Xy-pic diagram and the counted proof another one; both are delivered verbatim.
proof_roadmap: Read the failure of BC(f, n, q) as a property P of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over T.

Verify the three hypotheses: thickening-invariance by topological invariance of the etale site, stability under limits by the limit results for cohomology, and the decomposition property by restriction to a closed subscheme or its complement.
Apply the formal argument to obtain a field-valued point where the property still fails.
Read off the diagram and the sheaf annihilated by n witnessing the failure in degree q.
difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades a failure of base change in degree q to a counterexample over the spectrum of a field: assuming BC(f, n, q-1) holds but BC(f, n, q) does not, it produces a commutative diagram with T = Spec(K) and a sheaf on Spec(K) annihilated by n for which the base change map in degree q is not an isomorphism (statement lines 17078-17094, with the standing notation delivered as a context span from lines 16847-16866). The proof is an application of the same-chapter formal argument lemma, and its content is the verification of the three hypotheses for the property P that a scheme over T still carries a counterexample: thickening-invariance follows from topological invariance of the etale site (proof lines 17161-17164), limit-stability from the behaviour of pullbacks and cohomology under limits (proof lines 17167-17201), and the decomposition condition, which the author calls the most interesting, is proved by restricting the counterexample to a closed subscheme or to its quasi-compact complement (proof lines 17204-17293). The non-formal content is concentrated in that last verification. The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out verification, assembled by an explicitly cited formal principle.
